description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of various news outlets, likely representing their proportional share within a dataset related to narrative media framing in political discourse. The chart is divided into 18 distinct slices, which are visually arranged in descending order of size in a counter-clockwise direction, concluding with a final aggregated category. There is no separate legend; instead, each slice is accompanied by an external text label identifying the news source and an internal numerical label representing its value, which sums to 100 across the chart, suggesting these are percentages. The largest individual slice is labeled "Breitbart" (blue, 14), followed counter-clockwise by "Drudge Report" (orange, 8), "The Daily Caller" (green, 8), "The Huffington Post" (red, 7), "NPR" (purple, 6), "Vox" (brown, 6), "The Guardian" (pink, 5), "BBC" (grey, 5), and "RT" (yellow-green, 4). Continuing counter-clockwise, the chart displays a series of smaller slices, each labeled with a value of 3, which include "Daily Kos" (cyan), "National Review" (dark blue), "Daily Mail" (orange), "Red State" (green), "Fox News" (red), "CNN" (purple), "PoliticusUSA" (brown), and "Shareblue" (pink). Finally, an "Other" category (grey, 13) is positioned clockwise adjacent to the largest slice, completing the circle. None of the segments are visually emphasized through explosion, offset positioning, or bolded text.
